newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway stock down on profit-taking, Yeltsin rumour.
newsitem.headline: Norway stock down on profit-taking, Yeltsin rumour.

text.p: The Norwegian Total index followed the international lead on Thursday and closed lower on profit-taking after rising through seven consecutive sessions.
The index finished 0.23 percent lower at 869.60 in moderate turnover of 561 million crowns partly following unfounded rumours that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had died.
"The rumours of Yeltsin's death contributed to profit-taking after several days of bullish trade," one trader said.
Overnight in New York rumours Yeltsin had died were partly responsible for a fall in Wall Street stocks, according to analysts.

In Oslo, the shipping, industry, insurance and bank indexes all fell. Industrial giant Norsk Hydro, which has a 20 percent weighting on the Total index, closed 1.3 percent lower at 309 crowns. But industrial group Aker was up 2.33 percent at 132 crowns although it reported lower-than-expected 8-month profits.
"There are buyers, but no sellers in Aker," one broker said. "Nobody dares to sell in Aker because they are so anxious to find out what is going to happen."
The boards of Aker and investment group RGI on October 1 proposed to merge operations to create one of Scandinavia's largest industrial groups.
